title: Bluetooth applications: keyboards, audio, and internet limits

spans.text: Bluetooth can carry sensor data, act as an input device, provide a serial console, or stream audio to a speaker. Each job requires the right profile and chip.

Keyboard use has two distinct roles: as a HID device, an ESP32 sends key events to a computer; as a HID host, it receives input from a real keyboard. BLE-HID libraries and board support vary. Key events should follow deliberate, visible user actions; hidden or unauthorized keystroke injection is unsafe. An A2DP sink can connect an original Classic-Bluetooth ESP32 to an audio source; audible output usually also needs an I2S DAC/amplifier (for example MAX98357A) and a speaker. Software alone is not a speaker.

Bluetooth itself is not internet access. A phone/PC gets internet via Wi-Fi or cellular and may use Bluetooth to control the ESP32. Bluetooth tethering over PAN works only when the exact device, profile, operating system, and stack support a PAN role; standard BLE GATT does not create an internet tunnel. Wi-Fi STA is the normal ESP32 internet path.

spans.title: Important safety and compatibility note
spans.text: A2DP requires Classic Bluetooth and will not work on every BLE-capable ESP32. Check the library's chip support and I2S DAC wiring. Do not assume Bluetooth tethering is available on every phone or ESP32.
